name: dirb
one_line: web content scanner (guess directories and files)
plain: `dirb` takes a wordlist and tries each word as a path on a web server, then reports which ones exist. It is the simplest directory brute-forcer: one command, sensible defaults and recursive digging into every folder it finds.
It is slower and less flexible than gobuster or ffuf, but it is on every Kali install and is easy to remember.
when: Quickly find hidden folders and files on a lab web site.

examples.title: Default scan
examples.explain: Uses /usr/share/dirb/wordlists/common.txt and recurses into each directory it finds. Hits show CODE and SIZE.

examples.title: Another wordlist
examples.explain: The second argument is the wordlist.

examples.title: Add extensions
examples.explain: -X tries each word with every extension (and without).

examples.title: Do not recurse
examples.explain: -r stops it from digging into found folders, which is quicker.

examples.title: Silent, with a cookie
examples.explain: -S hides the tested word line; -c sends a cookie.

examples.title: With a delay
examples.explain: -z waits 100 milliseconds between requests to be gentler on the server.

options.plain: Wordlist (default common.txt); several files separated by commas.
Do not squash or merge /../ and /./ sequences.
Print the Location header on redirects.
Ignore responses with this status code.
Interactive recursion: ask before each folder.
Silent mode: do not show the tested word.
Do not force a trailing slash on URLs.
Do not stop on warning messages.
Extensions, or a file with extensions.

mistakes: Using only the small common.txt and concluding there is nothing there.
Forgetting -X and missing files such as admin.php.
Letting it recurse into a huge tree without a limit.
Running it against sites you are not authorised to test.
try: Run dirb on a lab server and write down every code 200 and 301 result.
Compare the speed of -r against the default.
see_also: gobuster(1), ffuf(1), wfuzz(1), nikto(1), curl(1), and the wordlists in /usr/share/dirb/wordlists.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
